figures.finding: From the 2024 tax year a resident pays nothing on the first FJD 30,000, 18% to 50,000, 20% to 270,000, then 33% rising one point per band to 38% from 500,000 and 39% above 1,000,000.
figures.applies: Tax years from 2024, in force until amended (so 2026).

sources.said: These income tax rates apply to Personal Income Tax assessments for resident individuals from the 2024 tax year onwards and will remain effective until amended by the Income Tax Regulations.
1,000,001 + $318,500 + 39% of excess over $1,000,000 Income Tax Rates for Non-Resident Individuals.

figures.finding: An employee contributes the mandated 8% of wages to the Fiji National Provident Fund and the employer a mandatory 10%; an employer contribution above the 10% is taxable pay.

sources.said: You can choose to pay more than the mandated 8% contributions from your wages to boost your FNPF savings,
Example excess FNPF, any amount of FNPF contribution exceeding the mandatory 10% employer contribution will be subject to PAYE and entered in the bonus column when filing payday.

figures.finding: A non-resident individual is taxed at 20% from the first dollar to FJD 270,000 and at the resident top rates above; a fee for professional or other independent services (and royalties) paid to a non-resident bears 15% non-resident withholding tax.

sources.said: 2026 15% Royalty, Management fee, Natural resource amount, fee for the provision of professional or other independent services
It is a tax withheld on sources that have been derived in Fiji for the provision of professional or other independent services.

figures.finding: VAT is 12.5% from 1 August 2025 (15% before), with a zero rate for listed items.

sources.said: Tax Year Tax Rate Effective Date 2025 0%, 12.5% 1st August 2025 2024 0%, 15% 1st August 2024

figures.finding: The employer withholds PAYE from a primary employment by the cumulative formula of reg. 6 of the Income Tax (Withholding Tax) Regulations 2013 (the year's tax on projected pay, less tax withheld to date), at a flat 20% on a secondary employment or where the employee has not lodged a tax code declaration within 5 working days, and pays it in by the last day of the next month.

value.primary: cumulative annualised formula (Withholding Tax Regulations 2013 reg. 6)
value.due: last day of the following month

sources.said: you are required to deduct tax at the no-declaration rate of twenty percent (20%) from your employee’s gross employment income. … The secondary rate of PAYE to be applied is twenty percent (20%) of the gross payment. … Income Tax to withhold = (A1/F × G) – B1 + Income Tax on C2 – Income Tax on C1 … The filing should no later than the last day of the month following the month to which the PAYE relates.

figures.finding: Tax years are calendar years (the 2017 rates split the year at 31 July and 31 December); an employee's or self-employed person's income tax return is due 3 months after the end of the tax year, so by 31 March.

value.returnDue: 3 months after the end of the tax year

sources.said: Income Tax • Employees or Representatives • PIT S (Employees) • Self-employed (i.e. farmers, consultants, taxi … • 3 months after end of tax year
Year of Assessment 2017 (1st August – 31st December 2017) … Year of Assessment 2017 (1st January – 31st July)

figures.finding: A business must register for VAT within 21 days of its gross annual turnover exceeding FJD 100,000; below that it may register voluntarily.

sources.said: Businesses must register for VAT with FRCS if their gross annual turnover is more than $100,000. • Businesses may voluntarily register for VAT if their gross annual turnover is below the threshold.
